Subject: Sable Labs — RAG discovery recap & proposed evaluation sprint

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off a short evaluation sprint. I pasted the high-level plan below and attached the one-pager + seed prompt set.

Recap (notes from today)
- Primary use case: internal engineering docs + release notes search for answers and task templates; high priority is accuracy for code snippets and links.
- Latency target: P95 < 550ms on short question paths; acceptable ~1s for long context retrieval.
- Data: ~120k docs (primarily markdown + PDFs), average doc size ~1.2 KB after chunking.
- Success criteria: grounding precision >= 92% on our 200-case eval set; hallucination rate < 3% measured by a combined human+automated check.

Recommended quick-start model & config (what I'd run first)
- Generation model: redwood/guide-13b-chat-q4f16 (balanced cost/quality for code + instruction following).
- Retriever: dense-embedding asymmetric retrieval (512-d vectors), index in Faiss HNSW, chunk size ~800 tokens (overlap 128).
- Reranker: cross-encoder reRanker-lite-v1 (fine-tuned on relevance pairs); use reranker for top-20 -> re-rank top-5.
- Caching: prefix caching enabled for repeated queries (engineering KB has high query repetition).

Proposed 2-week evaluation sprint (goals & artifacts)
- Week 0: access & ingest (we provide ingestion checklist; you share sample 10k doc export).
- Week 1: baseline runs — run three model-config variants (Guide-13B, Mistral-Instruct-7B, & a smaller 7B quantized) and collect metrics (latency, token cost, grounding precision).
- Week 2: focused QA on hallucination cases & prompt tuning; deliver final recommendation + prompt set and a short scoring report.

Benchmarks & artifacts (links attached)
- Seed prompt set: prompt_set_seed_001.jsonl (attached) for the 200-case human eval.
- Baseline notebooks & dashboards: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xAqSableLabs-RAG-eval

Open questions I noted
- Do you have any redlines on keeping raw docs in a vendor-managed index vs. customer-hosted vector DB?
- Procurement timeline for a small PO / trial commitment (we estimate 2–3k USD for the two-week run if you use hosted).

Attachments: Sable_RAG_eval_plan_v1.pdf, prompt_set_seed_001.jsonl

Next steps
- Can you share a 10k-document sample export by EOD Wed so we can schedule ingestion?
- If procurement needs a scope-of-work for a pilot PO, we can send a one-page statement of work.

Thanks — I’ll block time in the calendar for a kick-off after you share the sample.

—
Dev Patel

Alyssa / procurement team — answering each item inline: 

1) SOW / pricing: I attached a one-page SOW (PDF) and a conservative estimate for the 2-week sprint (hosted option ~2,800 USD; private connector option ~4,200 USD to cover staffing + storage). If you prefer, we can convert to an itemized PO line for your procurement.

2) Customer-hosted vectors: yes — Redwood supports customer-hosted vector stores via our private deployment connector. We can point ingestion at your S3 + Faiss index; we will run retrieval locally (in your VPC) and keep no copied raw docs in the Redwood-hosted index unless you opt-in.

3) Regression monitoring: during the sprint we propose: 
- Daily automated scoring on the 200-case seed set (we compute grounding precision, exact-match on snippets, and a semantic-similarity check for false positives).
- Weekly human spot-checks (30 random queries) targeting hallucination-prone categories (code snippets/URLs).
- Alerting: slack/email alerts on regression delta >3ppt grounding precision or hallucination rate increase >1.5ppt.

Kickoff windows: Jul 6 — 9am PT or Jul 6 — 2pm PT. Which works for you?

Attachments: Sable_RAG_eval_plan_v1.pdf (SOW), prompt_set_seed_001.jsonl
